    Finite submodules in the perpendicular of a presilting differential #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.invertedOn_iff_linear {R : Type u} [Ring R] (P : TwoTerm R) (N : ModuleCat R) :
    P.InvertedOn N ↔ Function.Bijective fun (f : ↑P.target →ₗ[R] ↑N) => f ∘ₗ ModuleCat.Hom.hom P.differential.hom
    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.exists_fg_invertedOn_ge (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] (P : TwoTerm R) (hp : P.IsPresilting) (N : ModuleCat R) (hn : P.InvertedOn N) (U : Submodule R ↑N) (hu : U.FG) :
    ∃ (V : Submodule R ↑N), U ≤ V ∧ V.FG ∧ P.InvertedOn ↧↥V

    Every finitely generated submodule of a module inverting a presilting differential is contained in a finitely generated submodule that inverts it.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.invertedOn_iff_perpendicular (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : FGModuleCat R) :
    P.InvertedOn M.obj ↔ Subsingleton (CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel P.differential ⟶ M) ∧ Subsingleton (M ⟶ nakayamaKernel k P)

    Inversion on a finite module is detected by the two Hom perpendiculars of the differential, for arbitrary projective terms and differential.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.invertedOn_iff_semistable (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (hp : P.IsPresilting) (M : FGModuleCat R) :
    P.InvertedOn M.obj ↔ (eulerWeight k P).IsSemistable M

    On finite modules, inversion coincides with semistability for the Euler weight.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.invertedOn_iff_directed_union_semistable (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (hp : P.IsPresilting) (N : ModuleCat R) :
    P.InvertedOn N ↔ ∃ (S : Set (Submodule R ↑N)), S.Nonempty ∧ DirectedOn (fun (x1 x2 : Submodule R ↑N) => x1 ≤ x2) S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ S, ∃ (x : Module.Finite R ↥V), (eulerWeight k P).IsSemistable ↧↥V

    An arbitrary module inverts a presilting differential precisely when it is a directed union of finite semistable submodules.
